newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves rates unchanged as unemployment rises.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves rates unchanged as unemployment rises.

text.p: The German central bank left all three of its key interest rates unchanged Thursday, as had been expected.

The Bundesbank's announcement came after news of a bigger-than-expected rise in German unemployment in October. But economists had argued that, given recent evidence of a steady economic upturn, the central bank had no reason to provide additional stimulus.

The discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at 3 percent for the next two weeks.
All 10 economists polled by Reuters this week said they expected the German central bank to keep rates on hold for the rest of the year.

While economists see little immediate threat of a slowdown in the economy, the Federal Labour Office warned that the upturn was not strong enough to curb unemployment significantly. It said average unemployment would stay at just under four million this year and next.
In October, unemployment rose by 41,000 people to a seasonally adjusted 4.04 million. The unadjusted unemployment rate was steady at September's level of 10.1 percent.
But recent economic indicators have shown that exports, helped by a weaker mark, are starting to pick up.
Exports have historically been the first part of the German economy to recover from slower periods, followed by an increase in investment and after that by increases in spending.
